title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in this 1986 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)' Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic, combinatorial framework for tame stratified spaces. There is a set L of 'lieux' (loci, the elementary pieces). A 'figure' F is a finite stratified object with set of strata F~. The relation G ≪ F means G is a subfigure of F. ombr(X) ('ombre', shadow) is the set of lieux lying in a stratum X, and ombr(X)° is its interior part, written x ⋘ X. The relation ∥ means disjoint, and ≭ means incompatible. The labels 'At 9', 'At 9'', 'At 10', 'At 11'' are numbered statements of the axiomatics.

Page 71 defines a discrete figure Φ as one all of whose strata are lieux (Φ~ ⊂ L). Such a figure is determined by the subset A = Φ~ ⊂ L. A finite subset of L is a figure iff its lieux are pairwise disjoint.

Corollary 4 (this page): let F be a figure and A ⊂ L. A defines a discrete figure 𝒢 with 𝒢 ≪ F iff two conditions hold.
(i) 𝒢 ⊂ ombr(F).
(ii) For every stratum X of F, 𝒢 ∩ ombr(X) 'is a figure', e.g. is finite and made of pairwise disjoint lieux.
In words, being a discrete subfigure is a local condition, checked stratum by stratum.

Grothendieck then remarks that the sufficient criterion At 9' for incompatibility X ≭ Y, which is stated in terms of the disposition of lieux, is in a sense also necessary. He calls this 'visiblement' a consequence of At 10.

Corollary 5: if G is a subfigure of F with G ≠ F, then there is a lieu x with x ⋘ F (x in the shadow of F) and x ∥ G (disjoint from G).
Proof sketch: G is a proper subfigure, so some stratum X ∈ F~ is not a stratum of G. Pick x in the interior shadow ombr(X)° (reference (148)). Disjointness from G then follows either from At 9 (criterion on the disposition of lieux) together with At 10 (criterion of disjointness), or from the construction of 'figured' neighbourhoods.
The result is a separation property: proper subfigures are detected by lieux. The next page uses such facts to strengthen At 11' on the compatibility of subfigures under the operations ∧ and ∨.
errors: The proof of Cor. 5 is only sketched. It needs that a lieu in the interior of a stratum not belonging to G is disjoint from all of G. That depends on G being a subfigure (union of strata of F) and on the frontier conditions of the stratification, which are only invoked by reference to At 9/At 10.
Cor. 4 (ii) is stated informally ('soit une figure', with the scare quotes in the original); finiteness of 𝒢 ∩ ombr(X) for each X plus finiteness of F~ yields finiteness of 𝒢.

ideas.what: Discrete subfigures of a figure are characterised by subsets of lieux satisfying a stratum-wise local condition.
ideas.modern_name: Finite sets of points compatible with a stratification (refinement of a stratification by adding point strata) in o-minimal / tame topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in o-minimal geometry (van den Dries); stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only calls for a 'topologie modérée'; the axiomatics of Analysis situs is unpublished

ideas.what: A proper subfigure G of F admits a lieu in the interior shadow of F that is disjoint from G.
ideas.modern_name: Separation / density of open strata: a point in the open part of a missing stratum avoids the closed subcomplex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard for stratified spaces / CW complexes

missed.claim: This page belongs to Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic 'analysis situs' of figures and lieux (1986), a synthetic tame-topology framework. Its individual results are routine, but the axiomatic system as a whole (At-axioms, the shadow 'ombre', the relations ≪, ⋘, ≭, ∥) is not documented in the literature.
missed.quote: Soit X ∈ F~ \ G~, et x ∈ ombr(X)° ... Je dis qu'il fait l'affaire.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of interest for comparing Grothendieck's tame topology programme with o-minimality and with combinatorial models of stratified spaces (exit-path categories, posets of strata).

deep.surprise_reason: Routine lemmas inside an unpublished axiomatic framework. The framework itself is only modestly notable, and nothing on this page is a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'formé de lignes deux à deux disjointes' should read 'formé de lieux deux à deux disjoints'.
'les conditions données en termes de disposition des lignes' reads 'disposition des lieux'.
At 9 and At 10 are described as criteria 'pour les lieux', not 'pour les lignes'.
In Cor. 5: 'Soient F une figure, G une sous-figure ≠ F'.
In Cor. 4 the subset is 'A de L' (L = set of lieux), with 𝒢 written above it as an insertion.
